body: Explain each in one sentence: (i) Intestate Succession Law; (ii) Alternative Dispute Resolution; (iii) patrilocal; (iv) primogeniture; (v) patrilineal inheritance; (vi) tenants-in-common.
answer:
> [!answer]
> (i) **Intestate Succession Law** (PNDC Law 111): the law that distributes the property of a person who dies **without a valid will** among the spouse, children, parents and family.
> (ii) **ADR**: settling disputes **outside the courts** through negotiation, mediation or arbitration.
> (iii) **Patrilocal**: a married couple lives with or near the **husband's** family.
> (iv) **Primogeniture**: inheritance by the **first-born (usually eldest son)**.
> (v) **Patrilineal inheritance**: property passes through the **father's line**.
> (vi) **Tenants-in-common**: co-owners each hold a **separate share** that passes to their own heirs on death (no survivorship).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Precise one-sentence definitions earn full marks.

## Simplified explanation

Know each term in one line.

body: (a) Distinguish between **civil marriage** and **customary/common-law** marriage. (b) Discuss **five** advantages of civil (ordinance) marriage in Ghana.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** **Civil (ordinance) marriage** is contracted under the **Marriages Act (Cap 127)** before a registrar or licensed minister; it is **monogamous** and requires court divorce. **Customary marriage** is contracted according to the **customs** of the families (knocking, bride-price); it is **potentially polygamous**. (A common-law/'living together' union has no formal rites.)
>
> **(b)** (1) **Legal recognition** and certificate as proof; (2) **monogamy** protects spouses; (3) clearer **property and inheritance rights** for spouse and children; (4) divorce only through the **courts**, giving protection; (5) easier access to benefits (pensions, insurance, visas); (6) **registration** helps national records.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Customary marriages can also be registered under PNDC Law 112.

## Simplified explanation

Statutory and monogamous vs customary and potentially polygamous; legal protection.

body: (a) Explain the concept of **marriage**. (b) Examine **five** relevances of marriage in Ghana.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** Marriage is a **socially and legally recognised union** between a man and a woman (and their families, in Ghana) that establishes rights and obligations between them, their children and their kin.
>
> **(b)** (1) **Legitimate procreation** and continuity of lineage; (2) **socialisation** of children; (3) **economic cooperation** and support; (4) **alliances between families**; (5) regulation of **sexual behaviour**; (6) social **status and identity**; (7) companionship and emotional security.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Marriage in Ghana is a union of families, not just individuals.

## Simplified explanation

A recognised union; procreation, socialisation, economics, alliances.
